entries.title: Ten source images establish the visible apartment.
entries.detail: Seven interior photographs, a dimensioned marketing floor plan, one exterior and one aerial. Room connections and listed dimensions anchor the model. Ceiling height, exact openings, bedroom assignment and unseen surfaces remain inferred.

entries.title: The first connected apartment.
entries.detail: A dedicated builder created walls and doorways, sliding windows, marbled floors, built-in robes, leather sectional, workstation, kitchen appliances, renovated bathroom, fans and balcony. The overview below records the first version.

entries.title: The bed and bath screen were oriented incorrectly.
entries.detail: A separate critic compared the model structure with the source images. The builder corrected the bed headboard to its short end and the bath screen to the exposed long edge. Bedroom mapping is explicitly described as inferred. Balcony access was also repaired.

entries.title: The living room needed softer fabrics.
entries.detail: The critic captured real living-room and kitchen renders before its session hit the account usage limit. The lead compared these with the photographs. Flat throws and rigid cushions were the clearest remaining visible weakness.

entries.title: Folded cloth, softer cushions and clearer room views.
entries.detail: The lead replaced flat throws with folded cloth and fringe, softened cushions, improved the living-room starting view, added an actual bathroom mirror, corrected wardrobe fronts and added fixture collisions. An ambient-occlusion experiment produced visible artifacts and was removed after inspecting the output. This is a direct comparison, not a blind independent A/B verdict.

entries.title: Eight accessible spaces, one connected model.
entries.detail: All eight starting positions are clear and connected on a 5 cm navigation grid against 62 collision surfaces. Type checking passes. The lead inspected real living, kitchen, bathroom and bedroom renders; original-photo mode and the floor-plan dialog work. A 390 px phone layout was inspected. Room navigation accepts valid inputs and rejects invalid rooms.

entries.title: The original quality bar is not met.
entries.detail: The spatial critic found a recognizable architectural reconstruction, but insufficient material detail, illumination and source fidelity for the requested photorealistic experience. The interaction critic verified room changes, orbit, look controls, source photos and the plan, and identified tiny phone navigation targets. Those phone controls now have a named room selector and larger movement buttons.

entries.title: This is a reconstruction, not a Gaussian splat.
entries.detail: Most rooms have only one photograph, which does not establish unseen geometry or a continuous photorealistic apartment. To reach scan fidelity, provide a slow overlapping walkthrough connecting all rooms, with translated views around objects and doorways under steady lighting. The garage remains unplaced, as the supplied plan explicitly says not in position.

entries.title: Door placement, sofa spacing and flat graphics need work.
entries.detail: You identified misplaced doors, a sofa obstructing entry, missing textures, and incomplete lighting and reflections. These issues reopen spatial and visual review; the current model is not presented as finished.

entries.title: The entry is clear and door swings follow the plan.
entries.detail: The sofa now leaves approximately 95 cm to the inside entry wall, 97 cm to the kitchen partition and 77 cm to the bedroom wall. Bedroom leaves swing into their rooms and the bathroom opening moves to the left half of its wall. Door and furniture collisions follow the corrected geometry. All eight room landings remain connected on the navigation grid; visual review remains separate. A later independent critique identified that bedroom openings belong in the corridor side walls; that correction remains outstanding.

entries.title: Marbled tile, patterned rug and charcoal leather.
entries.detail: Three material-only images were generated separately from the supplied photographs, then applied with appropriate tiling and subtle surface relief. These are AI-derived appearance maps, not measured texture scans. The original photographs remain available for direct comparison.

entries.title: Window light and reflections of the actual apartment.
entries.detail: Apartment-specific reflection captures and window lighting are applied. Window glass no longer casts opaque shadows. This is cached room radiance, not a physically baked GI solution. Independent final lighting review was interrupted; no quality-bar pass is claimed.

entries.title: Your park views now surround the apartment.
entries.detail: The three supplied screenshots were reconstructed into one wrapped panorama, with phone controls and arrows excluded. The balcony and bedroom renders were inspected. Timber uses a new reference-derived grain map; leather, tile and fabric surface response were adjusted. The panorama is approximate, with synthesized missing directions. Smaller public updates will make progress easier to inspect.

entries.title: Larger phone controls and properly scaled brick surfaces.
entries.detail: Walking buttons are 52 px, view controls 44 px, and full-screen mode works within the page. The 390 px layout has no horizontal page overflow. Rendering stops when the view is stationary or the page is hidden; coarse-pointer devices use smaller reflection captures and lower pixel density. Photo-derived brick is mapped at a consistent approximate physical scale on balcony and outward wall faces, with concrete balcony flooring and coping. Phone fullscreen and balcony renders were inspected; independent review was interrupted by the usage limit. Actual-device performance remains unmeasured.

entries.title: Both bedroom entrances now open from the corridor.
entries.detail: The builder moved both entrances to the corridor side walls, restored the bedroom front walls, and matched the inward swings to the plan. A separate critic verified the door topology. The lead inspected the rendered overview and all eight room landings remain reachable in the collision-grid check. Exact room dimensions and photographic fidelity remain under refinement.

entries.title: Botanical bedding and softer copper throws.
entries.detail: Two albedo maps were generated separately from the original photographs. An independent critic inspected actual room renders and identified overly dense flowers and overly orange throws; both were corrected. The final throw review found useful improvement with no visible seams or missing textures. Bedding and cushion geometry remain simplified. Texture loading retains successful materials if another image fails.

entries.title: Rearrange the apartment and keep your layouts.
entries.detail: Select and drag existing furniture, rotate in 15-degree steps, remove or replace it, and undo changes. Eleven library pieces include a padded channel-headboard bed with lofted pillows and draped bedding. Account-linked layouts are stored on the server, with file export and import. The newer upholstered-bed photo was not available, so that design is explicitly inferred.

entries.title: Brighter daylight, contact shadows and less uniform upholstery.
entries.detail: A separate critic compared actual living-room renders with both source photographs. The largest issues were rigid cushions and grey, uniform daylight. This pass adds cushion compression and folds, finer fabric texture, varied leather roughness, short-range ambient occlusion, softer shadow filtering and brighter window contribution. Furniture reflections refresh after edits. It remains a reconstruction: cushion silhouettes, specular highlights and missing viewpoints still differ from the photos.
